summary.title: Apple
summary.extract: An apple is the round, edible fruit of an apple tree. Fruit trees of the orchard or domestic apple, the most widely grown in the genus, are cultivated worldwide. The tree originated in Central Asia, where its wild ancestor, Malus sieversii, is still found. Apples have been grown for thousands of years in Eurasia before they were introduced to North America by European colonists. Apples have cultural significance in many mythologies and religions.

data.Name: Apple Inc.
data.Description: Apple Inc. is an American multinational technology company that specializes in consumer electronics, computer software, and online services. Apple is the world's largest technology company by revenue (totalling $274.5 billion in 2020) and, since January 2021, the world's most valuable company. As of 2021, Apple is the world's fourth-largest PC vendor by unit sales, and fourth-largest smartphone manufacturer. It is one of the Big Five American information technology companies, along with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook.

With Apple Inc gearing up for its biggest product launch of the year, the company is opening a lottery for US retail employees who want to help staff the in-person unveiling. The lottery allows retail employees to apply to work the event, where they’ll help organise lines, check in guests, greet attendees, offer directions and support the security teams, according to a memo that was seen by Bloomberg News. The launch event will take place during the first half of September, the company told staff, without providing a more specific date. Historically, Apple’s iPhone presentations have taken place on the second Tuesday or Wednesday of that month. Since Labour Day in the US falls on Monday, Sept 7, a Wednesday event appears slightly more likely, as it would preserve the workday travel window Apple has historically provided for attendees. In the memo, Apple said it was "excited to offer US store team members the opportunity to participate in the Event Support Experience Program.” A spokesperson for the Cupertino, California-based company declined to comment. Apple has relied on retail employees to help staff major product launches for years. Workers who participated in either this year’s Worldwide Developers Conference or last year’s iPhone launch aren’t eligible for the upcoming program. Interested employees must apply by Aug 8, and Apple will notify those selected by Aug 17, according to the memo. This year’s September event carries added significance. It will be the first major product unveiling under Chief Executive Officer John Ternus, who is set to take over from Tim Cook on Sept 1. OpenAI Group PBC has publicly pushed back against a lawsuit that Apple Inc. filed against it last month. The ChatGPT developer outlined its arguments in a blog post published on Monday. The move came shortly after Apple submitted a new court filing in connection with its litigation. In the document, the company asks the court for expedited evidence collection and a preliminary injunction against OpenAI. Apple filed its lawsuit last month. The complaint accuses OpenAI of stealing intellectual property from the iPhone maker to support its push into the consumer electronics market. According to recent reports , OpenAI plans to launch a line of AI-powered devices that will compete with the iPhone. The ChatGPT developer’s Monday blog post takes aim at several of the core arguments in the lawsuit. Notably, the company also published correspondence between its employees and Apple staffers. OpenAI says that the chat logs and emails weaken the iPhone maker’s arguments. The lawsuit accuses former Apple engineer Chang Liu of failing to return a company laptop before leaving for OpenAI. Furthermore, Apple claims that Liu downloaded dozens of internal files with sensitive product information. The complaint alleges that he accessed the files using a “rare, previously unknown authentication bug.” According to OpenAI’s blog post, the iPhone maker “now tries to shift the blame to ‘residual access.’” That’s a term for access permissions left active by accident. OpenAI claims that such permissions are a common issue at Apple. The lawsuit also names a second former Apple employee as a plaintiff. Tang Tan was the company’s vice president of product design before joining OpenAI last year.
